chapter: Bird's world, singers and the new music
title: Opposition to bebop
summary: Old players didn't want to change, critics didn't understand.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Of course, you had his appeal to the public with the singing and all that. But on the other hand, he was trying to bring this new music forth, and at that time, as you know, being in it, it had a lot of opposition. And that's something we could talk about...
Yes. Because people were against this music.

Oh yeah, they hated the newcomers. I don't know why. The old guys didn't want to learn nothing new. I guess that's basically what it really boils down to, is that they didn't want to change from their traditional things that they had been playing to play what the younger guys were playing. So I guess that's what really caused it to happen like that.
Of course, you took a lot of bad press.
Well, the only reason why they gave it bad press, they didn't understand it. And anything they don't understand, they don't like.

If you don't understand it, how are you going to like it? You know what I mean? You've got to first find out what it is, and then if you put it down, you have a right. You say, 'Well, I checked it out, and it ain't there,' you know. But if you do it right, and if it's there, you say, 'Yeah, it's there...' -- well, what else can you say?

But it also seemed that a lot of the bad publicity Bebop got was more about the way people dressed, or the drugs, or this-that-and-the-other-thing. People seemed to fix on those things to the exclusion of the music. The fact that Dizzy wore a beret and a leopard-skin jacket or whatever seemed to get more attention than what he was playing.
Yeah. Well, you know... Knowing Dizzy... If you know Dizzy, I mean, what else can you say? Because he just might do anything. They didn't name him 'dizzy' for nothing. He's something else, boy.
